newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity ends mostly down in late selloff.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity ends mostly down in late selloff.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures ended mostly lower Thursday in a late selloff after early gains due to ongoing plant outages and continued frigid weather in the Rockies and eastern Northwest.
"We saw some late selling pressure combined with profit taking," said an East Coast paper broker.

May California-Oregon Border (COB) futures settled up 13 cents at $11.93 a megawatt hour (MWh), trimming a 55 cent gain. June COB finished down five cents at $11.85 after posting a high of $12.30. Other active COB contracts ended eight to 30 cents lower.

May Palo Verde (PV) settled down five cents at $15.35, wiping out an early 35 cent gain. June PV finished up five cents at $16.45 after bouncing between $16.45 and $16.75. Active deferred PV months ended 15-21 cents lower.
Day-ahead firm, peak electricity prices at COB rose to $16.00-17.00 from yesterday's $14.75-15.75, while those at PV increased to $17.00-18.00 from $16.00-16.75 Wednesday.

In addition to cold weather and plant outages, the next-day market was bolstered by the absence of Bonneville Power Adminstration's (BPA) for the second day, and start of water spillage today at the hydroelectric dams on the Snake River, market sources said.
Brokers and traders are split about the direction of the complex tomorrow.

There is growing concern that cash prices, which have fueled nearby futures higher in recent sessions, would ease soon when temperatures in the West are predicted to climb next week, the East Coast broker said.
"It's going to continue to go up. We're just taking a breather," said a Houston futures trader, referring to today's late sell-off.

Separately, Pacific Gas and Electric Co raised the output at the 1,087 megawatt (MW) Diablo Canyon nuclear unit 2 to 75 percent of capacity after holding at 50 percent for several days due to feedwater pump maintenance.
A 408 MW unit at coal-fired Craig power station in Colorado was shut earlier this week for planned maintenance, and expected to resume operation April 23.
In the Rockies and eastern part of the Northwest, readings would run six to 12 Fahrenheit degrees below normal through Sunday. while those along the coast would average near normal.

Down in the Southwest, temperatures would average 10 to 15 degrees F below normal in the northern section and six to 12 degrees below normal in the southern portion. Readings would moderate toward normal levels by Sunday.
NYMEX estimated 353 COB and 288 PV contracts were sold, down from yesterday's 585 COB and 368 PV lots.
